title: Polling and downloading
description: Wait for completion, save bytes, and release storage.

sections.title: Poll until terminal
paragraphs: Read the job once per second in your own client, with an overall deadline. Stop at succeeded or failed. A 404 can mean expiration, deletion, or a job owned by a different key.
The workspace SDK polls every 250 ms and defaults to a 180-second client timeout. This timeout is separate from the worker timeout.

sections.title: Download authenticated bytes
paragraphs: After success, GET /v1/jobs/{id}/download returns application/octet-stream with an attachment filename of converted.<format>. Save it using your own output name. It is not a signed URL or JSON response.
A job produces one output. For PDF images, choose a page with the page option; use the local CLI for a multi-page batch.

sections.title: Delete when finished
paragraphs: DELETE /v1/jobs/{id} removes queued or completed jobs and files. Outputs otherwise remain until expiration.

sections.title: Use a deadline, not an unbounded loop
paragraphs: Choose a total wait budget that includes upload, queueing, and conversion. A two-minute worker limit does not guarantee that a queued job will finish within two minutes of creation. The SDK’s default client timeout is three minutes; it can be changed per call.
Poll only while the status is queued or running. Avoid simultaneous overlapping polls for one job. On transient network errors, apply bounded backoff; on a failed job, stop and report the failure.

sections.title: Save safely
paragraphs: Download using the same configured origin as the API and the same bearer token. The relative downloadUrl does not grant anonymous access. Avoid forwarding credentials to a URL supplied by an untrusted caller.

Write to a new output path or a temporary file that you rename after a complete download. If a network failure interrupts a download, retry while the job exists. A partial file on disk is not a successful conversion.
